title: 🌿 Essential Oils Guide
subtitle: More than just pleasant scents - practical uses for everyday life

intro.title: What You'll Learn
paragraphs: Essential oils aren't just for making things smell nice! In this guide, you'll discover practical, time-tested uses for essential oils in first aid, gardening, and around the house. From treating minor cuts to keeping pests away, these natural solutions have been helping families for generations.
Important: Always read the safety warnings at the bottom before using any essential oils.

items.title: Cuts & Abrasions
items.body: Tea tree oil can be used to help sterilize cuts. Always dilute properly and test on a small area first.

items.title: Insomnia
items.body: A few drops of Lavender oil on the underside or in the corners of your pillow can help promote a sound night's sleep.

items.title: Lice Prevention
items.body: Tea tree oil can be used in shampoo to kill lice, and in hair products to help prevent lice.

items.title: Pain Relief
items.body: Birch, eucalyptus and peppermint can all be used as a local anesthetic for minor aches and pains.

items.title: Rash & Irritation
items.body: Tea tree oil can soothe itch from bug bites, rash or poison ivy. Always dilute before applying to skin.

items.title: Sinus & Respiratory
items.body: Eucalyptus is used for its respiratory, sinus, and cold easing properties. Try adding to a diffuser or steam inhalation.

items.title: Basil Oil
items.body: Repels flies and supports vegetable plant health. Spray diluted solution around plants.

items.title: Cedarwood Oil
items.body: Use it to help prevent roaches, slugs and snails from damaging your garden plants.

items.title: Lavender Oil
items.body: Attracts beneficial pollinators like bees and butterflies while repelling mosquitoes and chiggers.

items.title: Peppermint Oil
items.body: Repels ants, aphids, beetles, moths and spiders. Perfect natural pest control.

items.title: Tea Tree Oil
items.body: Helps plants ward off diseases, mold and fungus. Great for plant health maintenance.

items.title: Thyme Oil
items.body: Deters beetles on rose bushes. Keep your beautiful flowers protected naturally.

items.title: Dishwasher Boost
items.body: Add two drops of grapefruit or lemongrass essential oil to your dishwasher before using it. The oil helps remove grease and soap accumulation so your dishes shine.

items.title: Flea Repellent
items.body: Lemongrass oil can be used to repel fleas. Add about five drops to a cup of water in a spray bottle, then lightly spray your pet's coat.

items.title: Rodent Deterrent
items.body: Dab a few drops of peppermint oil on cotton balls and place them around your home, or make a spray with two teaspoons of oil for every one cup of water.

items.title: Rug Freshener
items.body: Add 12 drops of lavender oil to one ounce of baking soda. Mix and sprinkle on the rug, let sit for 30 minutes, then vacuum.

items.title: Stinky Shoes
items.body: Dab a few drops of your favorite essential oil on two cotton balls, place one in each shoe, and leave overnight.

items.title: Tick Prevention
items.body: Lavender oil can repel ticks and makes it difficult for the eggs to hatch. Add a few drops of lavender oil to the shampoo of your pet.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Important Safety Warnings
paragraphs: Never ingest: Essential oils may be toxic if ingested, never swallow or ingest essential oils.
Wash hands: Wash hands after handling essential oils, as residue on the fingers may damage contact lenses or cause eye discomfort.
Patch test first: When using on skin or pet, start with a patch test to make sure you do not have an allergic reaction.
Read labels: Always read the labels and adhere to any recommendations provided.
Dilute properly: Most essential oils should be diluted with a carrier oil like coconut or jojoba oil before applying to skin.

footer.heading: Thanks for learning with Grandma! 🌿
footer.text: Remember: Always use essential oils safely and consult professionals for serious health concerns.
